nodes.d: The fourfold order 'created according to the division of guṇa and karma' (4.13) — qualities and work, which the Gita describes in terms of inner nature (18.41–44).
nodes.sub: वर्ण · Social Order by Guṇa & Karma
nodes.text: The fourfold order 'created according to the division of guṇa and karma' (4.13) — qualities and work, which the Gita describes in terms of inner nature (18.41–44). varṇa Social Order by Guṇa & Karma

nodes.d: Action, and the moral law of action. 'Karma is the creative force that brings beings into existence' (8.3); its course is 'unfathomable' (4.17).
nodes.text: Action, and the moral law of action. 'Karma is the creative force that brings beings into existence' (8.3); its course is 'unfathomable' (4.17). karma Action

nodes.d: The subtle teaching that the wise 'see inaction in action and action in inaction' (4.18) — freedom is not abstention but non-doership.
nodes.text: The subtle teaching that the wise 'see inaction in action and action in inaction' (4.18) — freedom is not abstention but non-doership. akarma Inaction-in-Action

nodes.d: Action performed as duty without craving for its fruit: 'Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits' (2.47). The heart of Karma Yoga.
nodes.text: Action performed as duty without craving for its fruit: 'Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits' (2.47). The heart of Karma Yoga. niṣkāma karma Desireless Action

nodes.d: Union through selfless, skilful action offered to the Divine — 'yoga is skill in action' (2.50). Krishna's answer to Arjuna's wish to escape the battlefield.
nodes.text: Union through selfless, skilful action offered to the Divine — 'yoga is skill in action' (2.50). Krishna's answer to Arjuna's wish to escape the battlefield. karmayoga Yoga of Action

nodes.d: Relinquishing the fruit of action while still acting — distinguished from saṃnyāsa (giving up action) in 18.2, and declared the true renunciation (18.11).
nodes.text: Relinquishing the fruit of action while still acting — distinguished from saṃnyāsa (giving up action) in 18.2, and declared the true renunciation (18.11). tyāga Renunciation of Fruits

nodes.d: Formal renunciation of action. The Gita reinterprets it inwardly: the true saṃnyāsī neither hates nor desires (5.3) and performs duty without depending on its fruit (6.1).
nodes.text: Formal renunciation of action. The Gita reinterprets it inwardly: the true saṃnyāsī neither hates nor desires (5.3) and performs duty without depending on its fruit (6.1). saṃnyāsa Renunciation

nodes.d: Action as offering. 'Work done as yajña does not bind' (3.9); Chapter 4 widens yajña to knowledge, breath, study and self-restraint, culminating in 'brahmārpaṇam' (4.24).
nodes.text: Action as offering. 'Work done as yajña does not bind' (3.9); Chapter 4 widens yajña to knowledge, breath, study and self-restraint, culminating in 'brahmārpaṇam' (4.24). yajña Sacrifice & Offering

nodes.d: Giving — sattvic when given as duty, at the right place and time, to a worthy recipient, expecting nothing in return (17.20).
nodes.text: Giving — sattvic when given as duty, at the right place and time, to a worthy recipient, expecting nothing in return (17.20). dāna Charity

nodes.d: Disciplined heat of effort — austerity of body, speech and mind (17.14–16), sattvic when undertaken with faith and without desire for reward.
nodes.text: Disciplined heat of effort — austerity of body, speech and mind (17.14–16), sattvic when undertaken with faith and without desire for reward. tapas Austerity

nodes.d: Direct, liberating knowledge of reality. 'There is no purifier in this world like knowledge' (4.38); its marks are humility, non-violence, patience and the rest (13.8–12).
nodes.text: Direct, liberating knowledge of reality. 'There is no purifier in this world like knowledge' (4.38); its marks are humility, non-violence, patience and the rest (13.8–12). jñāna Liberating Knowledge

nodes.d: Knowledge made experiential — jñāna together with vijñāna, 'knowing which nothing more remains to be known' (7.2, 9.1).
nodes.text: Knowledge made experiential — jñāna together with vijñāna, 'knowing which nothing more remains to be known' (7.2, 9.1). vijñāna Realised Wisdom

nodes.d: The veil over knowledge that deludes beings (5.15). 'The ignorant, the faithless and the doubting soul perish' (4.40).
nodes.text: The veil over knowledge that deludes beings (5.15). 'The ignorant, the faithless and the doubting soul perish' (4.40). ajñāna Ignorance

nodes.d: The contemplative path of discrimination between the Self and not-Self — one of the 'two paths' Krishna described of old (3.3).
nodes.text: The contemplative path of discrimination between the Self and not-Self — one of the 'two paths' Krishna described of old (3.3). jñānayoga Yoga of Knowledge

nodes.d: The analytical understanding of Self and matter that Krishna teaches first (2.11–30) before turning to the yoga of action (2.39).
nodes.text: The analytical understanding of Self and matter that Krishna teaches first (2.11–30) before turning to the yoga of action (2.39). sāṃkhya Discriminative Insight

nodes.d: The person whose wisdom is established — content in the Self, unshaken by sorrow, free of craving, fear and anger. Portrayed in eighteen verses (2.55–72) answering Arjuna's question (2.54).
nodes.text: The person whose wisdom is established — content in the Self, unshaken by sorrow, free of craving, fear and anger. Portrayed in eighteen verses (2.55–72) answering Arjuna's question (2.54). sthitaprajña One of Steady Wisdom

nodes.d: One who has gone beyond sattva, rajas and tamas — the same in pleasure and pain, praise and blame, honour and dishonour (14.22–26).
nodes.text: One who has gone beyond sattva, rajas and tamas — the same in pleasure and pain, praise and blame, honour and dishonour (14.22–26). guṇātīta Transcender of the Guṇas

nodes.d: The body-mind is the 'field'; the conscious witness who knows it is the 'knower of the field' (13.2–3) — the analytical heart of Chapter 13.
nodes.text: The body-mind is the 'field'; the conscious witness who knows it is the 'knower of the field' (13.2–3) — the analytical heart of Chapter 13. kṣetra-kṣetrajña The Field & Its Knower

nodes.d: Loving devotion to the Divine. 'Whoever offers me with love a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water — that I accept' (9.26); the beloved devotee is described in 12.13–20.
nodes.text: Loving devotion to the Divine. 'Whoever offers me with love a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water — that I accept' (9.26); the beloved devotee is described in 12.13–20. bhakti Devotion

nodes.d: Union through unwavering love — the theme of Chapter 12, where Krishna names those 'ever-united, endowed with supreme faith' as the most perfect in yoga (12.2).
nodes.text: Union through unwavering love — the theme of Chapter 12, where Krishna names those 'ever-united, endowed with supreme faith' as the most perfect in yoga (12.2). bhaktiyoga Yoga of Devotion

nodes.d: Devotion with no other refuge. 'To those who worship me with undivided minds, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have' (9.22).
nodes.text: Devotion with no other refuge. 'To those who worship me with undivided minds, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have' (9.22). ananya bhakti Undivided Devotion

nodes.d: Taking refuge in the Divine. Arjuna begins as a disciple who has 'surrendered' (2.7); Krishna's final word is 'abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone' (18.66).
nodes.text: Taking refuge in the Divine. Arjuna begins as a disciple who has 'surrendered' (2.7); Krishna's final word is 'abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in me alone' (18.66). śaraṇāgati Surrender & Refuge

nodes.d: The Divine's compassionate grace that dispels darkness from within (10.11) and by which the devotee attains the eternal abode (18.56).
nodes.text: The Divine's compassionate grace that dispels darkness from within (10.11) and by which the devotee attains the eternal abode (18.56). anugraha Divine Grace

nodes.d: Constant remembrance, especially at life's end: 'whatever state one remembers on leaving the body, to that one goes' (8.6). 'Remember me and fight' (8.7).
